title: Unit Economics Scenario Lattice — October 2025
content:
Purpose:
This workbook-style note documents a compact scenario lattice for evaluating combined headcount phasing, capacity (GPU equivalent units), and pricing sensitivity. Goal is to give product + finance + strategy a short, tradeable surface we can run quick pivot analysis on when pricing or demand signals change.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Build a 3x3x3 lattice: Pricing tier delta, HC phasing (frontloaded / linear / backloaded), and capacity utilization (low/nominal/high).
- Compute per-token marginal cost, contribution margin, and EBITDA delta across 18-month horizon.
- Primary levers: price per 1k tokens, percent of requests eligible for prefix-KV caching, and batch-size uplift.
- Use this lattice to generate trigger recommendations for: marketing promos, committed capacity purchases, and HC hiring pauses.

Key assumptions (base-case where not stated):
- Base price (hosted API average realized price): $0.018 per 1k generation tokens (mix of text + multi-turn chat).
- Base embedding price: $0.004 per embedding (per 1k dims normalized unit) — embeddings are modeled separately in sheet tab 'Embeddings (summ)'.
- Avg request tokens generated per invocation: 340 tokens.
- Fraction of requests that are cacheable (prefix match) base: 18%.
- GPU equivalent cost to Redwood (amortized + infra + power + SW): $1.45 per 1M tokens served at nominal utilization (includes dedicated & shared infra blended).
- Headcount cost per new FTE on average (fully loaded): $280k/year (inc. benefits, options refresh, bench).
- HC ramp time (when hiring): 6 months to full productivity; partial productivity at month 3 (~55%).
- Planning horizon: 18 months (Oct 2025 — Mar 2027).

Lattice design (how to interpret):
- Pricing delta (3 levels):
  * P- = -15% from base (aggressive promo / low-price test)
  * P0 = base price (as above)
  * P+ = +20% from base (value capture test / enterprise upsell)
- HC phasing (3 profiles):
  * HC-Frontloaded = hire 60% of planned HC in Q1 of horizon, then 40% distributed later (aggressive hiring to support new product lines).
  * HC-Linear = steady hire across 6 quarters to target headcount.
  * HC-Backloaded = delay hiring until Q3, concentrate hires in second half (cash-constrained posture).
- Capacity utilization (3 bins):
  * Low = 55% utilization average (higher per-token cost due to idle infra)
  * Nominal = 78% utilization average (current target)
  * High = 92% utilization (strong demand / efficient batching)

Primary outputs calculated per scenario cell:
- Blended marginal cost per 1k generation tokens (cost_token) — includes GPU, network, storage caching overheads, and per-request infra costs.
- Contribution margin per 1k tokens = price_per_1k - cost_token.
- Monthly EBITDA delta across horizon vs baseline.
- Cash runway impact (months saved/consumed) given a fixed burn-rate profile.
- Sensitivity to a 10pp change in cacheable requests and to a 10% change in batching efficiency.

Representative numeric example (single cell):
Scenario: P+ (price +20%), HC-Backloaded, High utilization
- Effective price per 1k tokens = $0.0216
- Utilization uplift reduces GPU-equivalent cost to $1.15 per 1M tokens -> cost_token = $0.00115 per 1k tokens (GPU only)
- Adding infra+ops overheads per 1k tokens = $0.0009 -> blended cost_token = $0.00205
- Contribution margin = $0.0216 - $0.00205 = $0.01955 per 1k tokens (~90.6% margin)
- Monthly net impact vs base price: assume volume grows 8% m/m; monthly incremental EBITDA becomes positive at month 2 given delayed HC.

Headcount phasing logic (spreadsheet implementation notes):
- Columns: Month, Planned hires (by role bucket: serving/runtime/infra/product/ops), Onboarded FTEs, Effective productivity multiplier, Labor expense (monthly), Recruiting lag (time to offer -> start = 45 days assumed).
- For cash math, we model hiring ramp cost across both payroll and one-time recruiting + hiring tool costs ($9k per hire).
- To estimate headcount impact on unit cost, we map FTEs into two buckets: capacity-facing (ops/infra/runtime) and non-capacity (product/eng/core). Only capacity-facing headcount materially reduces per-token cost through better utilization, queuing, and SRE optimizations.

Pricing sensitivity surface insights (derived from lattice):
- Small price reductions (<=10%) materially increase demand in SMB segments (elasticity ~ -1.8 in our micro-seg tests) but compress margin faster than volume recovers for embedding-heavy workloads.
- Price increases (+15-25%) for enterprise tier show low elasticity (~ -0.3) when matched with committed-capacity discounts; net revenue increases and lowers unit cost by smoothing utilization.
- Promotions targeted at high-cache customers produce asymmetric benefits: volume grows but marginal cost drops more than revenue — profitable.

Trigger rules (operationalized):
- If utilization >85% for 3 consecutive weeks AND queue latency above 95th percentile by 40ms -> recommend accelerated HC + capacity reservation (move to HC-Frontloaded scenario).
- If gross margin per 1k tokens falls below 55% for 2 months -> pause promotional pricing and run A/B to identify elastic segments to revert.
- If projected 12-month run-rate EBITDA heads negative by >5% vs forecast -> freeze non-critical hires and delay major capacity purchases by 2 quarters.

Appendix (quick formulas implemented in sheet):
- monthly_tokens = baseline_monthly_tokens * (1 + volume_growth_rate) ^ months
- gpu_cost_per_1k = (amortized_gpu_monthly_cost / effective_monthly_served_tokens) * 1000
- blended_token_cost = gpu_cost_per_1k + infra_per_1k + ops_per_1k - cache_savings_per_1k
- contribution_margin_pct = (price_per_1k - blended_token_cost) / price_per_1k

Next steps / requests to reviewers:
- Finance: sanity-check fully-loaded FTE rate and recruiting cost assumptions for FY26 comp plan changes.
- Product: validate which curated segments we can target for cache-friendly promotions (list top 5 customers by prefix recovery ratio).
- Infra/Serving-runtime: provide empirical utilization-to-cost mapping for high-utilization scenario (we used a conservative 20% cost drop from nominal; request real data).
- Sales/RevOps: confirm elasticity numbers for enterprise commitments (we used -0.3 estimate).

Short TODO (practical):
- Convert this note into a two-tab sheet: (1) Lattice matrix generator (scenario input -> outputs) (2) Headcount phasing schedule with automated cash waterfall.
- Hook linked JIRA tickets for scenario experiments to tracking board: JIRA-FIN-2032 (already linked).
- Schedule run with Product + Infra to re-run lattice after retrieving real utilization curves (target by 2025-11-10).

Quick provenance notes:
- Pulls partial numbers from FY26 planning doc and last quarter's infra runbook; aims to remain conservative on cost savings until infra validates production delta.
- This is intentionally compact / heuristic — use as decision support, not a final budget commit.
